;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**Unidentified gunmen [[kidnap]] 10 [[humanitarian aid]] workers in southwestern [[Niger]], their [[NGO]] reports. Gunmen in the area have previously stolen several vehicles from the [[International Committee of the Red Cross]] and [[Médecins Sans Frontières]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/armed-group-abducts-10-aid-workers-southwestern-niger-200625152015498.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Iraqi insurgency (2017–present)]]
**[[Iraqi security forces]] raid the [[headquarters]] of the [[Iran]]ian-backed [[Kata'ib Hezbollah]], detaining three high-ranking commanders of the group, and at least 20 other fighters. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-security/iraqi-security-forces-raid-iran-backed-militia-headquarters-government-sources-idUSKBN23W3J9 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*At least 100 people are killed by [[lightning strike]]s as a [[monsoon]] storm batters [[India]]'s northeastern states of [[Bihar]] and [[Uttar Pradesh]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-lightning/lightning-strikes-kill-over-100-in-two-indian-states-idUSKBN23W2ZC?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo]]
****Health officials in the Democratic Republic of the Congo say the number of cases reached 6,411 there with 198 new infections in the past 24 hours. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/covid-19-cases-fatalities-continue-to-spread-in-africa/1890276 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Central African Republic]]
****In the [[Central African Republic]], the number of infections climbs by 88 in the past 24 hours to reach 3,051. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/covid-19-cases-fatalities-continue-to-spread-in-africa/1890276 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iraq]]
***Iraq confirms 107 new deaths from the virus, bringing the death toll to 1,437. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/health/iraq-records-107-fresh-covid-19-fatalities/1890275 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The U.S. reports 37,077 cases, the largest number of new cases in a single day. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/25/health/us-coronavirus-thursday/index.html (CNN)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
***Portuguese government orders the lockdown of 19 districts of [[Lisboa]] despite the end of the "calamity status". [https://www.politico.eu/article/almost-700000-portuguese-face-new-corona-lockdown/ (''Politico'')]
*[[Kivu Ebola epidemic]]
**The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] announces the end of the second outbreak of [[Ebola]] in the country, which has killed more than 2,200 people. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-ebola-congo/congo-announces-end-of-ebola-outbreak-in-east-second-deadliest-on-record-idUSKBN23W1LP?il=0 (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[Kosovo]] formally designates [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] political party [[Hezbollah]] and its [[paramilitary]] wing as a [[terrorist organization]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/world/2020/06/25/Kosovo-declares-Hezbollah-s-political-military-wings-as-terrorist-organization- (Al Arabiya)] 

;Law and crime
*[[Rasmus Paludan (politician)|Rasmus Paludan]], leader of the [[Far-right politics|far-right]] [[Denmark|Danish]] political party [[Hard Line (political party)|Hard Line]], is sentenced to prison for one month for a string of offences, including [[hate speech]], [[defamation]] and [[dangerous driving]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53185194 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[War crimes in the Kosovo War]]
**[[Kosovo]] [[Prime Minister of Kosovo|Prime Minister]] [[Avdullah Hoti]] cancels his trip to the [[United States]] where talks between Kosovo and [[Serbia]] were to be held, after his country's [[President of Kosovo|President]] [[Hashim Thaçi]] is indicted by the [[Kosovo Specialist Chambers and Specialist Prosecutor's Office]] on [[war crime]]s charges. Thaçi also canceled his trip to mediate with Serbia after learning of the indictment the day prior. [https://apnews.com/dc601cc07f2869a5642922449b3de006 (AP News)]
*[[2020 Russian constitutional referendum]]
**After having been postponed once due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia|COVID-19 pandemic]], voting about [[2020 amendments to the Constitution of Russia|potential amendments]] to the [[Constitution of Russia]] kicks off. The result of the [[referendum]] might, amongst other changes, prolong the mandate of [[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]]. Voting continues until the 1st of July. [https://www.dw.com/en/russians-vote-on-constitutional-changes/a-53931760 (DW)]
*The [[Leader of the Labour Party (UK)|Leader]] of the UK's [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]], [[Keir Starmer]], [[dismissal (employment)|sacks]] his [[Shadow Secretary of State for Education]] [[Rebecca Long-Bailey]] for sharing an article on [[social media]] that says American police were trained by [[Mossad]] to use the knee-on-neck restraint that [[Killing of George Floyd|killed]] [[George Floyd]], which [[Israeli police]] say is false. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-53183085 (BBC News)]

;Sports
*[[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup]]
**[[FIFA]] announces that the 2023 Women's World Cup will be [[Australia–New Zealand 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup bid|jointly hosted]] by [[Australia]] and [[New Zealand]]. [https://www.fifa.com/womensworldcup/news/australia-and-new-zealand-selected-as-hosts-of-fifa-women-s-world-cup-2023tm (FIFA)]
*[[2019–20 Premier League]]
**[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] become [[Premier League]] champions for the first time and win their first top-flight title since the [[1989–90 in English football|1989–90 season]], after rivals [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] fail to win against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in a 2–1 defeat at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53183857 (BBC Sport)]
